$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Signatures extension 0.1.0 (proposal), written against Core v1.3 rev. 11 and reference files 5.2.0, portable verification 0.1.0, action binding 0.2.0 and anchoring 0.2.0. Binds only an implementation that says it uses this extension.
title: Signatures attachment
description: The person's signatures and the organisation's seals, each an object beside the records, the export or the attachment it concerns, and, optionally, independent timestamps over their signature values (anchoring 0.2.0's assertion, by reference). The attachment never adds a field to a record, an export or an action-binding attachment. It carries key references only: never a key or a certificate, since a verifier takes every source of trust from its own trust policy, which is anchoring 0.2.0's.

stage_id.description: A stage identifier as action binding 0.2.0 writes it.

time.description: A time signed as text: UTC, to the second, in exactly this form (the shared rule). It is a real UTC time with no leap second: a verifier reports a time it cannot read as failed.

signature.description: The signature over the signed bytes the verifier builds from the assertion's fields. The key comes from the verifier's trust policy, never from the attachment. Ed25519 signs the signed bytes themselves. WebAuthn-ES256 (a passkey) signs authenticatorData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON), where clientDataJSON's challenge is the SHA-256 of the signed bytes; both are carried so that the verifier can check them.

key_ref.description: A key reference names one key. The key, its holder and its role come from the trust policy.

value_b64.description: The signature value in padded base64: 64 bytes for Ed25519; the DER ECDSA-Sig-Value the authenticator returns for WebAuthn-ES256.

authenticator_data_b64.description: WebAuthn-ES256 only: the authenticatorData the authenticator signed, as returned.

client_data_json_b64.description: WebAuthn-ES256 only: the clientDataJSON bytes the client made, as returned. Its challenge is the SHA-256 of the signed bytes, in base64url with no padding.

person_signature.description: The person's own signature over what they decided. One of three assertion types, each with one fixed field order under the shared rule: person_approval and person_review for an outcome recorded under action binding, person_affirmation for a Core record that has no action binding.

person_approval.description: An approval: the outcome stage, what the review showed (the specification's digest and, when the review states one, the view's digest) and the approved digest. The outcome is signed, so a signed rejection cannot be presented as an approval.

stage_id.description: The outcome stage, in the action-binding attachment of this record.

shown_view_digest.description: The review's view digest, when it states one. Absent, the field is signed as the empty byte string.

signed_at.description: The time the signer states. It is signed, and it is the signer's statement, not independent time.

person_review.description: A rejection or an escalation: the outcome stage and what the review showed. It carries no approved digest.

person_affirmation.description: The affirmation of a Core record that has no action binding: the digest of the record's covered bytes, which are the bytes the Standard seals (the seal field absent or zeroed as portable verification states, affirmation_record as it stands in them). That digest is the record's seal_hash.

organisation_seal.description: The organisation's seal: the issuer's key over exactly what it issued. sealed names what is sealed (an export, an action-binding attachment or a record), its identifier and its digest: the export's or the attachment's bytes as issued (with an embedded copy of the seal replaced by A), or the record's seal_hash. The signature is Ed25519 in 0.1.0; another algorithm is reported as not supported.

id.description: The decision_id of a record or of an action-binding attachment; the issuer's reference for an export, which states no identifier of its own.

sealed_at.description: The time the issuer states. It is signed, and it is the issuer's statement, not independent time.

timestamp.description: An independent timestamp over a signature value: anchoring 0.2.0's timestamp assertion, by reference. The token's messageImprint is the SHA-256 of the raw signature value. The subject names an assertion of this profile as anchoring 0.2.0 names it (the same objects its attachment schema admits for a signature subject of this profile), so that one attachment can carry the timestamps of both; this attachment carries timestamps over this profile's assertions only.

of.description: The assertion whose signature value this is: its type, its key reference and what it names (the decision_id, and for an outcome its stage_id, or what a seal seals). profile, when given, names this profile.

tsa_ref.description: A reference to the time-stamping authority. Its certificate comes from the verifier's trust policy, never from the attachment or the token.

token_b64.description: The DER bytes of the RFC 3161 TimeStampToken, in padded base64.
